note: Recast from Oshima 1914; the original is in English and does not describe the alate. The measurement head length (with mandibles) 2.84—3.06 appears in the original as 2,843, 06, a comma misprinted for a dash.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellow, mandibles brown with paler bases, abdomen straw yellow; head sparsely hairy, abdominal tergites densely hairy. Head oval; base of the clypeus short and poorly separated from the frons, its apical part short and squarish, anterior angles rounded; labrum lingulate, apex pointed, not reaching the middle of the mandibles; mandibles sword-shaped, ending in an incurved spine-like point, the left mandible with a sharp tooth on the cutting edge near the middle and the right mandible with a reduced tooth in the same position; antenna 17 segments, segment 2 as long as segments 3 and 4 together; postmentum rectangular, 3 times as long as wide, slightly narrowed anteriorly; pronotum narrower than the head, saddle-shaped, with both the anterior and posterior margins medially concave, the anterior margin bilobed and raised. Measurements (mm): body length 6.80; head length (with mandibles) 2.84—3.06; head length (without mandibles) 1.72—1.88; head width 1.50—1.66; pronotum width 1.00—1.13, length 0.59—0.72.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Major worker: head yellow, abdomen white; head sparsely setose, abdominal tergites with a row of setae along the posterior margin. Head round; fontanelle indistinct; base of the clypeus markedly inflated; antenna 17 segments, segment 2 slightly longer than 3; anterior margin of the pronotum bilobed and slightly raised. Measurements (mm): body length 4.50; head width 1.47; pronotum width 0.84. Minor worker: antenna 17 segments, segment 2 as long as segments 3 and 4 together; anterior margin of the pronotum slightly concave medially. Measurements (mm): body length 4.00; head width 1.00; pronotum width 0.69.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Localities: Maros (1913-3-25), Menado (1913-5-19) and Peer Island (date unknown), all collected by Kanehira. The original notes that the alate is unknown and that the head capsule of the soldier varies greatly in size, but intermediate forms occur, so two castes cannot be separated.
